# Reprobuild

> Reprobuild (`repro`, v0.2.25, Apache-2.0) combines BuildXL's monitored automatic dependency tracking, Nix's pinned toolchains in a content-addressed store with atomic generations, and Terraform's plan-and-apply state reconciliation into one compile-time-checked Nim DSL (`repro.nim`, `home.nim`, `system.nim`) across Linux, macOS and Windows. Every link below resolves to a standalone Markdown (`.md`) topic file so an agent can load only the topic its current task requires.

Reprobuild models the workspace as a directed acyclic graph (DAG) of type-checked actions defined in the **`repro.nim`** DSL. Sibling repositories declared as **`repos/*.toml`** fragments in the workspace root (whose policy lives in **`repro-workspace.toml`**) are routed dynamically using **`repro develop`** (develop-mode). Build hermeticity is enforced using the **`librepro_monitor_shim`** user-space filesystem interceptor, and execution is cached locally through a per-edge disk store fronted by a host-wide **shared-memory grow-only index** that every engine inserts into directly. Package toolchains are concretized using a **`clingo`** solver, and background services are orchestrated using **`servicePlaceholder`** declarations.

## Non-Interactive CLI Rules for Agents

When invoking `repro` from an automated tool call (with no interactive TTY):

- **Run commands inside the project environment with `repro exec -- <cmd> [args...]`** — never invoke `repro shell`, which opens an interactive subshell and blocks non-TTY callers.
- **Request structured output with `--json`** (or `--format=json` on `capabilities`): `repro version --json`, `repro health --json [--offline]`, `repro graph --json`, `repro why <target> --json`, `repro show-conventions --json`, `repro stats overview --json`, `repro pressure --json`.
- **Preview host or account changes before applying**: run `repro infra plan` before `repro infra apply --plan <id>`, and `repro home plan` before `repro home apply`.
- **Never hand-edit generated lock or scan files**: update `repro.lock` with `repro lock update [<dep>]` or `repro lock refresh`, and update `repro.scanned-deps.nim` with `repro deps refresh`.

## Agent Topic Guides (Load Only the Topic You Need)

- [Reprobuild Intro for Agents (Start Here)](./docs/agents/Repro-Intro-for-Agents.md): Core architecture keywords, non-interactive CLI rules (`repro exec`, `--json`), binary pair (`repro` + `reprobuild`), and lock-pin refusal guardrails.
- [Idiomatic Reprobuild (Before Editing `repro.nim`)](./docs/user-guide/idiomatic-reprobuild.md): Action granularity, narrow declared inputs vs `io-mon` observation, collections, non-determinism, and common agent anti-patterns.
- [Test History, Timings, and RunQuota Store](./docs/agents/Test-History-And-Timings.md): Querying test durations, peak RSS, and exit signals from the host-wide RunQuota observation store.
- [Profiling Reprobuild Workloads](./docs/agents/Profiling-For-Optimization.md): Measuring scheduler, cache, and build-action bottlenecks accurately before optimizing.
- [How Reprobuild Replaces Bazel, Buck2, BuildXL, and Tup](./docs/agents/Replaces/How-Repro-Replaces-Build-Systems-Like-Bazel-Buck2-BuildXL-and-Tup.md): Type-checked DAG actions, `librepro_monitor_shim` hermeticity, and shared-memory action cache index.
- [How Reprobuild Replaces Nix, direnv, devenv, Spack, Conan, and Process Compose](./docs/agents/Replaces/How-Repro-Replaces-Environment-and-Service-Managers-Like-Nix-Direnv-Devenv-and-Process-Compose.md): Clingo-solved package constraints, locked dev-env overlays, and `servicePlaceholder` daemon orchestration.
- [How Reprobuild Replaces direnv (`repro allow` Trust Model)](./docs/agents/Replaces/How-Repro-Replaces-Direnv.md): Zero-bypass environment activation, closure-hash `repro allow` verification, and CI `REPRO_DEV_ENV_AUTO_ALLOW=1`.
- [How Reprobuild Replaces Just and Make](./docs/agents/Replaces/How-Repro-Replaces-Task-Runners-Like-Just-and-Make.md): Declaring and invoking named automation tasks (`repro tasks`, `repro run`) inside the locked dev environment.
- [How Reprobuild Replaces repo and Git Submodules](./docs/agents/Replaces/How-Repro-Replaces-Workspace-Managers-Like-Repo-and-Git-Submodules.md): Multi-repository manifests (`repro-workspace.toml`, `repos/*.toml`), branch roles, and `repro develop` routing.
- [How Reprobuild Replaces Local Terraform and Dotfile Managers](./docs/agents/Replaces/How-Repro-Replaces-Local-Infrastructure-Provisioners-Like-Terraform.md): Declarative `home.nim` and `system.nim` state resources, `plan`/`apply`, and atomic generation rollbacks.

## Getting Started

- [Reprobuild documentation](./docs/users/content/index.md): Reprobuild combines BuildXL's monitored dependency tracking, Nix's pinned store and generations, and Terraform's plan-and-apply state reconciliation into one compile-time-checked build and system graph.
- [Install reprobuild](./docs/users/content/install.md): Install repro on Linux, macOS or Windows through your package manager, Nix, Scoop or a release archive, and check that it runs.
- [Build your first project](./docs/users/content/tutorials/first-build.md): Build a project with a library and a program, change the library, and add a package that reprobuild finds from your imports.

## Concepts and Architecture

- [How reprobuild works](./docs/users/content/concepts/how-reprobuild-works.md): How Reprobuild combines BuildXL's monitored dependency graph, Nix's content-addressed store and generations, and Terraform's plan-and-apply reconciliation from one project file up to ReproOS and fleets.
- [Conventions and the three modes](./docs/users/content/concepts/conventions-and-modes.md): Why most projects need little or no project file, how reprobuild chooses between a project's layout, its ecosystem manifest and its project file, and when to move from one mode to another.
- [Dependencies and the store](./docs/users/content/concepts/dependencies-and-the-store.md): How a project names the tools and libraries it depends on, how reprobuild chooses one version of each, and where it keeps what it obtains.
- [How caching stays correct](./docs/users/content/concepts/how-caching-stays-correct.md): What reprobuild checks before it reuses an action's result, why an input nobody declared still counts, and what happens when that check cannot be made.
- [Tests and certificates](./docs/users/content/concepts/tests-and-certificates.md): How reprobuild runs tests as part of the build graph, splits a suite across machines, and records which content passed which tests.
- [Resources and state](./docs/users/content/concepts/resources-and-state.md): How a project declares resources of types any repository can define, as Terraform uses providers, and how reprobuild reconciles them, records their state and leases them to the tests that use them.
- [Machines and profiles](./docs/users/content/concepts/machines-and-profiles.md): How a profile describes your account or a whole operating system, how repro infra plans and applies it as Terraform does, and how each change becomes a generation you can roll back.
- [Fleets and the deploy agent](./docs/users/content/concepts/fleets-and-the-deploy-agent.md): How every machine in a fleet keeps the state you declare for it, by fetching a signed manifest and applying it with the same steps as repro infra apply.

## How-To Guides

- [Build an existing project](./docs/users/content/guides/building/build-an-existing-project.md): Build a Cargo, Go or CMake project with reprobuild by adding a short project file next to its existing manifest.
- [Enter a project's environment](./docs/users/content/guides/environments/enter-a-project-environment.md): Start a shell with a project's tools and variables, run one command inside its environment, choose an activity, or print the environment for another tool.
- [Diagnose your setup with repro health](./docs/users/content/guides/troubleshooting/diagnose-with-repro-health.md): Run reprobuild's environment check, read each failure and its remedy, apply the safe fixes automatically, and use the check in CI.
- [Join a workspace](./docs/users/content/guides/workspaces/join-a-workspace.md): Clone a multi-repository workspace onto a new machine, choose which of its projects to check out, and keep every repository current.
- [Build a repository from its layout](./docs/users/content/guides/building/build-a-monorepo-from-its-layout.md): Build a repository arranged as apps/<name>/ and libs/<name>/ with no project file, and check what reprobuild inferred from it.
- [Activate environments when you change directory](./docs/users/content/guides/environments/activate-on-directory-change.md): Install reprobuild's shell hook so a project's environment switches on when you enter its directory and off when you leave, and grant or withdraw trust per directory.
- [Work on a dependency's source](./docs/users/content/guides/workspaces/develop-a-dependency.md): Check out one of your repository's dependencies next to it, build your repository against your changes to it, and return to the locked revision when you are done.
- [Keep an existing Nix flake as the environment](./docs/users/content/guides/environments/keep-a-nix-flake-environment.md): Activate a repository's existing flake dev shell through reprobuild, without changing the flake and without direnv.

## Coming From Other Tools

- [Coming from Nix](./docs/users/content/coming-from/nix.md): How flakes, derivations, dev shells, the store and generations map onto reprobuild, what works differently, and when Nix is the better choice.
- [Coming from Bazel and Buck2](./docs/users/content/coming-from/bazel-and-buck2.md): How BUILD files, targets, rules, actions and caches map onto reprobuild, what works differently, and when Bazel or Buck2 is the better choice.
- [Coming from direnv, devenv and mise](./docs/users/content/coming-from/direnv-devenv-and-mise.md): How per-directory environments, tool versions, tasks and processes from direnv, devenv and mise map onto reprobuild, and when those tools are the better choice.
- [Coming from just and make](./docs/users/content/coming-from/just-and-make-tasks.md): How just recipes and make targets used as a task runner map onto reprobuild's tasks and build actions, and when just or make is the better choice.
- [Coming from repo and git submodules](./docs/users/content/coming-from/repo-and-git-submodules.md): How Google's repo manifests and git submodules map onto reprobuild workspaces, what works differently, and when repo or submodules are the better choice.
- [Coming from Terraform and OpenTofu](./docs/users/content/coming-from/terraform-and-opentofu.md): How Terraform's plan-and-apply model carries over to reprobuild's operating-system profiles and fleets, what works differently, and why Terraform or OpenTofu remains the tool for cloud resources.
